title: PA workflow spec exists with all required top-level keys
check_description: pa_workflow.yaml is submitted and contains the required top-level structure: product, payer_segments, workflow_steps, appeals, patient_support, and kpis.
score_1_criteria: File exists and all six top-level keys (product, payer_segments, workflow_steps, appeals, patient_support, kpis) are present.
score_0_criteria: File missing, or any of the six required top-level keys absent.
specific_file_locations: copeland_engagement_standards.md Part A defines the two deliverables and the machine-readable workflow spec; the required top-level shape is spelled out in the task brief.

title: Workflow steps: at least 12 fully-specified steps
check_description: workflow_steps has at least 12 objects and each carries the required fields (step_id, name, actor, system, inputs, outputs, sla_business_days, failure_paths).
score_1_criteria: At least 12 workflow_steps objects, and at least 85% of them carry non-empty step_id, name, actor, system, inputs, outputs, sla_business_days, and failure_paths.
score_0_criteria: Fewer than 12 steps, or the required per-step fields are missing/empty on more than 15% of steps.
specific_file_locations: The task brief enumerates the required steps (intake through adherence follow-up). pa_denial_reason_codes.csv and the hub thread supply failure_paths and hub-service steps.

title: Payer segments cover all four segments with required fields
check_description: payer_segments includes the commercial, Medicare, Medicaid, and uninsured segments, and each object carries the required per-segment fields.
score_1_criteria: At least 4 payer_segments; segment values cover commercial, medicare, medicaid, and uninsured; at least 75% of objects carry segment, share_pct, benefit_design, pa_required, expected_first_pass_approval_pct, turnaround_days_standard, turnaround_days_expedited.
score_0_criteria: Fewer than 4 segments, any of the four required segments missing, or the required fields missing on more than 25% of segment objects.
specific_file_locations: gpp_claims_extract_2025.csv gives the four-segment payer mix; payer_coverage_matrix.csv gives per-segment PA fields (benefit_type, pa_required, first_pass, turnaround).

title: Benefit design correct: pharmacy benefit and Medicare Part D
check_description: The workflow routes Solvara on the pharmacy benefit (Part D for Medicare) — the benefit_design values are 'pharmacy benefit' for the insured segments, the spec references Part D, and the strategy names the pharmacy benefit.
score_1_criteria: payer_segments benefit_design values contain 'pharmacy', with the phrase 'pharmacy benefit' appearing at least 3 times in pa_workflow.yaml (once per insured segment, per the controlled vocabulary); pa_workflow.yaml references 'Part D'; market_access_plan.md uses the phrase 'pharmacy benefit'.
score_0_criteria: Segments routed to medical benefit / buy-and-bill (fewer than 3 'pharmacy benefit' usages in the spec); or no Part D reference; or the strategy never names the pharmacy benefit.
specific_file_locations: solvara_product_profile.md: 'it adjudicates on the pharmacy benefit, and Medicare coverage is provided under Part D'. medicare_partd_coverage_determination_brief.md confirms self-administered drugs run under Part D. Trap: junior memo's buy-and-bill / Part B J-code.

title: Appeals ladder has at least three levels
check_description: The appeals section defines at least three levels and includes an external/independent review or peer-to-peer step.
score_1_criteria: appeals has at least 3 level objects; pa_workflow.yaml references at least one of peer-to-peer, external review, independent review/IRO, or Part D redetermination.
score_0_criteria: Fewer than 3 appeal levels, or no external/independent/peer-to-peer escalation defined.
specific_file_locations: medicare_partd_coverage_determination_brief.md describes the redetermination/IRE ladder; pa_denial_reason_codes.csv and the field-intel email describe peer-to-peer and pended-for-notes denials.

title: Patient support: hub, 30-day bridge, and copay program present
check_description: patient_support defines hub_services, a bridge_program set to the hub vendor's 30-day / two-fill parameter (not the deck's 90 days), and a copay_program.
score_1_criteria: patient_support.hub_services, patient_support.bridge_program, and patient_support.copay_program all present, and bridge_program.duration_days is 30 (per the hub vendor design thread).
score_0_criteria: Any of hub_services, bridge_program, or copay_program missing; or the bridge duration carries the deck's 90 days (or any value other than 30).
specific_file_locations: hub_vendor_design_thread.eml: 'The bridge should be up to 30 days, two fills max' plus the $20,000 commercial-only copay program. Trap: launch_strategy_deck_v3.md's 90-day bridge.

title: KPIs: at least five with target and rationale
check_description: kpis has at least 5 objects, each carrying kpi, target, and rationale.
score_1_criteria: At least 5 kpis objects, and at least 90% carry non-empty kpi, target, and rationale.
score_0_criteria: Fewer than 5 KPIs, or missing target/rationale on more than 10% of KPI objects.
specific_file_locations: The task brief requires kpis with kpi/target/rationale (e.g. first-pass approval rate, time-to-first-fill, PA turnaround compliance, appeal overturn rate, abandonment rate, adherence/PDC).

title: Headline figure: addressable population triangulated to ~4,125
check_description: The addressable US GPP population is reported as ~4,125 (7,500 diagnosed x 55% candidate fraction) in claims.json and the strategy — not the diagnosed 7,500 or the deck's 12,000.
score_1_criteria: claims.json key_figures.us_addressable_patients in [3700,4700]; and market_access_plan.md states a number in [3700,4700] on a line about addressable/eligible/candidate/treatable patients.
score_0_criteria: Reported as ~7,500 (diagnosed), 12,000 (deck), or outside the band; or the claims.json value is outside [3700,4700].
specific_file_locations: epi report '~7,500 patients (range 6,800-8,200)'; claims extract treated fraction ~54%; advisory board [00:22:40] '55%, are realistic candidates'. 7,500 x 0.55 = ~4,125. Traps: 7,500 (diagnosed), 12,000 (deck).

title: Headline figure: blended first-pass PA approval ~56%
check_description: Blended first-pass PA approval across insured lives is reported as ~56% (share-weighted from the coverage matrix and payer mix) in claims.json and the strategy — not the deck's 80% or analog B's 70%.
score_1_criteria: claims.json key_figures.blended_first_pass_pa_approval_pct in [0.52,0.60]; and market_access_plan.md states a value in [0.52,0.60] on a first-pass/approval line.
score_0_criteria: Reported as ~80% (deck) or ~70% (analog B), or outside the band; or the claims.json value is outside [0.52,0.60].
specific_file_locations: payer_coverage_matrix.csv first_pass by segment (commercial 62, Medicare 55, Medicaid 40); claims extract weights (55/22/18); (0.55*0.62 + 0.22*0.55 + 0.18*0.40)/0.95 = 0.562. Advisory board [00:31:15] 'high 50s blended, not the 80s'. Traps: 0.80, 0.70.

title: Headline figure: blended gross-to-net erosion ~42%
check_description: Blended gross-to-net erosion is reported as ~42% in claims.json and the strategy, consistent with the pricing memo — not the deck's rosier ~30%.
score_1_criteria: claims.json key_figures.blended_gross_to_net_pct in [0.38,0.46]; and market_access_plan.md states a value in [0.38,0.46] on a gross-to-net/net-price line.
score_0_criteria: Reported as ~30% (deck), or outside the band; or the claims.json value is outside [0.38,0.46].
specific_file_locations: gross_to_net_pricing_memo.md: 'blended gross-to-net erosion of approximately 42%'. Trap: launch_strategy_deck_v3.md 'roughly 30% gross-to-net erosion'.

title: Payer mix resolved: commercial ~55%, not 70%
check_description: The strategy reports the commercial payer share as ~55% (per the claims extract and epi), rejecting the launch deck's 70%.
score_1_criteria: market_access_plan.md states a value in [0.50,0.60] on a line about the commercial segment/payer mix.
score_0_criteria: Commercial share reported as ~70% (deck) or otherwise outside [0.50,0.60].
specific_file_locations: gpp_claims_extract_2025.csv payer mix Commercial 55%. Trap: launch_strategy_deck_v3.md '70% commercial'.

title: Distribution resolved: limited network of ~4 specialty pharmacies
check_description: The strategy recommends a limited distribution network of ~4 specialty pharmacies, rejecting the deck's open distribution across 15.
score_1_criteria: market_access_plan.md states a number in [3,5] (digits or spelled out) immediately followed, within three words, by specialty pharmacies / SPs / pharmacies, on a line about specialty pharmacy / SPs / distribution / network.
score_0_criteria: Recommends open distribution / ~15 SPs, or a number outside [3,5] on the distribution line.
specific_file_locations: specialty_pharmacy_network_options.csv: 4 rows selected=Y. Trap: launch_strategy_deck_v3.md 'open distribution across 15 specialty pharmacies'.
v1_change: E5-D07: the network count must be the number of pharmacies (identifier digits such as 'Q3' no longer count; v1 engine), and the in-band number must be followed by 'specialty pharmacies'/'SPs'; the line context also accepts 'distribution'/'SPs' (table rows such as '| Distribution model | Limited, 4 SPs |').

title: Benefit-type trap: no buy-and-bill in the workflow spec
check_description: The machine-readable workflow does not adopt the junior memo's buy-and-bill / Part B model — a pharmacy-benefit workflow contains no buy-and-bill billing steps.
score_1_criteria: pa_workflow.yaml has at least one workflow step; no workflow step name, actor or system contains buy-and-bill or buy-and-billing (any spelling), 'J-code' or 'medical benefit'; no payer segment benefit_design and no product.benefit_type contains 'medical benefit', 'Part B' or buy-and-bill (any spelling). Naming the junior memo's buy-and-bill model elsewhere in the file in order to reject it (e.g. 'medicare_pathway: Part D (not Part B buy-and-bill)') does not fail.
score_0_criteria: The workflow adopts buy-and-bill / medical-benefit routing: a workflow step is a buy-and-bill, J-code billing or medical-benefit step, or a segment's benefit_design / the product's benefit_type is medical benefit, Part B or buy-and-bill; or the workflow has no steps at all.
specific_file_locations: Trap: junior_analyst_access_memo.md 'set up as a buy-and-bill product... under the medical benefit, with Medicare reimbursing under Part B via a J-code'. Authoritative: solvara_product_profile.md self-administered subcutaneous -> pharmacy benefit.
v1_change: E5-D01/E5-D08/E5-D09: whole-file text_absent (which failed correct rejections that named the trap, passed '{}', and missed adoption phrased as 'medical benefit'/'J-code') replaced by the path-scoped spec proposed by the 2026-10 mapping audit (a13_v1_proposal) plus a non-vacuity gate; score text rewritten to match the op. 2026-10-08 token revision (E5-50): the step legs also catch 'buy-and-billing' (the v1 word boundary on 'bill' let it pass), and the benefit legs' bare 'medical'/'buy' are narrowed to 'medical benefit', 'Part B' and buy-and-bill, so a pharmacy benefit with a medical-exception process or a plan buy-in passes.

title: Strategy substance: required market-access topics covered
check_description: market_access_plan.md covers the required substance: payer mix/segmentation, prior authorization, specialty pharmacy distribution, patient support/hub, gross-to-net economics, step therapy, and appeals.
score_1_criteria: The strategy contains language on each of: payer mix/segmentation; prior authorization; specialty pharmacy; patient support/hub; gross-to-net; step therapy; appeals.
score_0_criteria: Any of the required topics absent from the strategy document.
specific_file_locations: The engagement standards scope the strategy to cover segmentation, PA, distribution, patient support, pricing/GTN, and coverage-policy navigation (step therapy, appeals).
v1_change: E5-D06/E5-D09: payer leg accepts 'segmentation' / 'payer landscape' (the brief's own wording); hyphenated forms ('prior-authorization', 'specialty-pharmacy') match through v1 token normalization.

title: WAC anchored at $150,000, not analog B's $180,000
check_description: The plan states Solvara's US WAC (list price) as $150,000 per patient per year — the figure in Veloxa's gross-to-net pricing memo and product profile — not the $180,000 carried by the analog biologic B coverage-policy excerpt.
score_1_criteria: market_access_plan.md states Solvara's WAC as $150,000 (or an equivalent list-price amount within $145,000-$155,000, e.g. '$150K') on the same line as WAC / list price / wholesale acquisition cost.
score_0_criteria: No in-band WAC amount on a WAC/list-price line, e.g. the plan carries $180,000 (analog B's list price) as Solvara's WAC, or states a list price outside $145,000-$155,000.
specific_file_locations: gross_to_net_pricing_memo.md: 'Solvara planned WAC is $150,000 per patient per year.' analog_coverage_policy_biologicB.md (trap): 'wholesale acquisition cost of approximately $180,000 per patient per year' — that figure belongs to the analog, not Solvara.
v1_change: E5-D06: '$150,000' anywhere in the plan no longer passes; the amount must sit on a WAC/list-price line (same line, scale words honoured). The unchecked net-economics clause was dropped from score_1 (it was never machine-checked).

title: Copay legal constraint: government beneficiaries excluded
check_description: The copay program is designed as commercially-insured only, with federal healthcare program beneficiaries excluded per the Anti-Kickback Statute, and government-insured/uninsured patients routed to an independent foundation or the PAP — rejecting the junior memo's copay-to-all proposal.
score_1_criteria: pa_workflow.yaml has patient_support.copay_program; every statement inside copay_program that mentions Medicare / Medicaid / government / federal beneficiaries carries an exclusion, ineligibility or foundation/PAP-routing cue; the workflow states the exclusion (commercially insured only / not eligible / federal healthcare program); and market_access_plan.md uses the anti-kickback / federal-healthcare-program / government-beneficiary exclusion framing.
score_0_criteria: Copay assistance offered to Medicare/Medicaid/government-insured patients (per the junior memo), e.g. 'eligibility: all patients including government-insured'; or the government-exclusion constraint never stated; or no copay program.
specific_file_locations: compliance_legal_copay_brief_thread.eml: copay 'may not be offered to any federal healthcare program beneficiary — Medicare, Medicaid, or TRICARE... routed to an independent charitable foundation or the PAP, never the copay card.' Trap: junior_analyst_access_memo.md 'offer the $0 copay card to every patient, including Medicare and Medicaid'.
v1_change: E5-D06: the bare token 'government' let a plan that OFFERS copay to government-insured patients (the illegal trap) pass; v1 adds a polarity-aware structured_polarity leg over copay_program and drops the polarity-blind token.

title: Step therapy handled: exception path for acute GPP, statutory turnaround honored
check_description: The deliverables treat step therapy as a barrier to be overcome via a documented step-therapy exception (appropriate for acute GPP presentation), not a design constraint to accept, and build PA SLAs to the statutory turnaround floor (standard 7 calendar days in most statute states, 10-14 in FL/MO/TN; 72-96-hour expedited) rather than the plan-quoted 15 business days. Judged against the advisory-board and statute sources.
score_1_criteria: The strategy and/or workflow explicitly build a step-therapy exception path for GPP and set PA turnaround SLAs consistent with the statutory floor, citing the advisory board and the statutes file; the plan-quoted 15-business-day SLA is treated as a compliance escalation, not the target.
score_0_criteria: Step therapy accepted as a required gate with no exception path, or SLAs built to the 15-business-day plan quote in statute states, or the acute-GPP clinical rationale ignored.
specific_file_locations: advisory_board_transcript_payer_md.md: 'lead with a step-therapy exception, not accept the step'. analog_coverage_policy_biologicA.md: 'trial and failure of at least two conventional systemic agents' (the barrier). state_pa_turnaround_statutes.csv: standard 7 days / 72-hour expedited. Trap: field_intel_payer_thread.eml '15 business days'.
